chapter_title: Concerning the Eighteen Great Thrones of all the Fathers
chapter_note: The chapter is largely a systematic, numbered cosmological list (18 thrones: 9 in the outer aeons, 9 in the zone) — this is strongly CORE in voice and structure. It is wrapped by a hagiographic/frame opening (¶1) and concluding doxological/summarizing material (¶11, ¶18), and it culminates in an explicitly institutional-hagiographic identification of the ninth throne in the zone with the present apostle in the holy church (¶17), consistent with the chapter-level editorial-fatigue drift.

paragraphs.core_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again he speaks to his disciples:" (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a formulaic dialogue attribution (FRAME), then immediately shifts into impersonal, numbered cosmological architecture (18 thrones; 9/9 division), which is characteristic of the older systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [...] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [...] apart. This is the first throne [...] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic enumeration and ontological description of a cosmic principle (Father/aeons), without audience address or institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered throne list; emanational cosmology in impersonal expository voice. (Page marker removed.)

paragraphs.core_text: The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first Enmity, which existed in the worlds of Darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core Manichaean/Iranian cosmological actors (First Man) in a functional, mythic-cosmic register; no ecclesial application.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered cosmological list; ‘Beloved of the Lights’ is treated as a cosmic hypostasis within the aeons.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a ...] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the Enemy and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process/function description (building the new aeon; prison/binding for the Enemy) stays entirely within cosmic mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: [The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of Darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world [s ...] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the Enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Strongly core: standard Manichaean cosmological role-description (rescue; ordering; construction; cleansing/binding) in impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered throne list with cosmic titles/functions (‘king of the zone’) — internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Although flagged ‘christian’ by vocabulary, ‘Jesus the Splendour’ here functions as a defined cosmological being (releaser/redeemer) within the Manichaean hierarchy, not as a Gospel citation.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind, he to whom] … and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional clause: "all the churches shall gather;" as an ecclesial pointing (cosmos → contemporary church-structure). Kept the throne identification and the cosmic/soteriological return of purified life.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core throne enumeration is present, but the phrase ‘all the churches shall gather’ shifts the mapping toward institutional referents; likely an editorial application grafted onto a cosmic identification.
Summative/doxological closure (‘for ever and ever, amen’) reads as editorial framing rather than the bare teaching list.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, these are the other nine thrones that are appointed in this world of the zone.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural transition within the same enumerative teaching (9/9 division); remains inside cosmological geography (‘world of the zone’).

paragraphs.core_text: Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic triadic placement (ships/day) — classic correspondential-architectural listing.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Iteration formula (‘Once again’) continues the internal cosmological mapping (night-ship; named hypostases). (Page marker removed.)

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Firmament-location mapping remains cosmological; no institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological mechanics (judge + three paths) presented as cosmic process/structure, not moral exhortation or church rule.
Explicit institutional and time-anchored application (‘apostle in the holy church’, ‘has come to you at this time’) is hagiographic/editorial self-identification, not substrate cosmology.
Fragmentary concluding summary with honor-language reads like an editorial wrap-up to the list rather than a needed element of the cosmological enumeration.
